To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the use of a common region-of-interest (ROI) design and the universal standardization of the ROI placement on different devices can reduce the interdevice variation of forearm BMD measurements.

(a) the use of a common ROI design reduces interdevice variability in forearm bone mineral density measurements, and (b) universal standardization of the ROI further reduces interdevice variability, and is thus an effective method for reducing interdevice variability in bone density measurements.
the manufacturer-implemented ROI is not optimal and that the universal standardization of the ROI can further reduce the differences between devices.

the standardization of the measurement of forearm BMD by DXA.
the improvement of interdevice comparability of BMD measurements, and the development of a common ROI that is easy to implement on all devices.
the standardization of DXA at the forearm.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a common ROI is the most effective method to improve interdevice comparabilities, followed by universal standardization of manufacturer-implemented ROIS.
standardization of the forearm BMD measurement should be done by implementing a common ROI and by universal standardization of the ROI location and size.

universal standardization and common ROIs should be implemented on all devices.
a combination of a common ROI with universal standardization is the best strategy for improving interdevice comparability for forearm BMD.

universal ROI standardization is a good way forward to improve comparability between devices, and a common ROI such that described here can be implemented as a standard for forearm measurements on all devices to achieve the best possible comparability.
